import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_99/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_99/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN on "city"
# Both tables have a "city" column, join on this column
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="city", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by on Source2_99_0.city and aggregation sum(Source2_99_0.driver_count)
# After join, the "city" column is unique, and driver_count is from df0 (Source2_99_0)
# Group by city and sum driver_count
df_grouped = df_joined.groupby("city", as_index=False)["driver_count"].sum()

# Ensure the schema matches target schema: ['city': string, 'driver_count': integer]
# Convert city to string (if not already) and driver_count to int
df_grouped["city"] = df_grouped["city"].astype(str)
df_grouped["driver_count"] = df_grouped["driver_count"].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_99/target_multisource.csv"
df_grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_99/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_99/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (inner join by default)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by city and aggregate driver_count by max (driver_count is unique per city in source0)
result = joined.groupby("city", as_index=False).agg({"driver_count": "max"})

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_99/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
